examples.en: We live in a small villa building.
This villa building has no elevator.
Monthly rent is cheaper in a villa than in an apartment.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 새로 지은 빌라로 이사했어요.
examples.en: My family moved into a newly built villa building.
There isn't enough parking in front of the villa building.

examples.ko: 친구는 삼 층짜리 빌라의 이 층에 살아요.
examples.en: My friend lives on the second floor of a three-story villa building.

explain: 영어의 villa처럼 별장이나 큰 저택이 아니에요. 한국에서는 아파트보다 작은 낮은 층의 공동주택을 '빌라'라고 불러요. 큰 단지로 지은 '아파트'와 구별해서 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike the English word villa, it doesn't mean a vacation home or a big mansion. In Korea, '빌라' is a low-rise residential building smaller than an apartment block. People use it in contrast with '아파트', which are built as big complexes.

examples.en: I unlock my phone with a password.
Yesterday I changed my screen lock password.

examples.ko: 잠금 버튼이 고장 나서 수리를 맡겼어요.
examples.en: The lock button broke, so I had it repaired.

examples.ko: 잠금 화면에 미리보기가 나오지 않도록 설정을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: I changed the settings so previews don't show on the lock screen.
Every app has a lock feature.

examples.ko: 중요한 서류는 잠금장치가 있는 서랍에 넣어 두세요.
examples.en: Please keep important documents in a drawer with a lock.

explain: '잠그다'의 명사형이고, 휴대폰·앱·화면처럼 기기에서 많이 나와요. 반대말은 '잠금 해제'이고, '잠금을 풀다'라고도 해요. 문이 스스로 잠기는 건 '잠기다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is the noun form of '잠그다' and appears a lot with devices like phones, apps and screens. The opposite is '잠금 해제', and you can also say '잠금을 풀다'. When a door locks by itself, you use '잠기다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling entered law school this year.

examples.ko: 로스쿨을 졸업하면 변호사 시험을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you graduate from law school, you can take the bar exam.

examples.ko: 저는 로스쿨에 가려고 대학교에서 열심히 공부했어요.
examples.en: I studied hard at university to go to law school.

examples.ko: 로스쿨 수업은 읽을 자료가 정말 많대요.
examples.en: I heard law school classes have a lot of material to read.

examples.ko: 친구가 로스쿨 입학 면접을 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend is preparing for the law school admission interview.

examples.ko: 로스쿨에 다니는 언니는 밤늦게까지 도서관에 있어요.
examples.en: My older sister, who attends law school, stays at the library until late at night.

explain: 정식 이름은 '법학전문대학원'이지만 일상에서는 거의 '로스쿨'이라고 해요. 법을 공부해서 변호사 같은 법조인이 되려는 사람이 다니는 대학원이에요. '로스쿨생', '로스쿨 입시'처럼 다른 말과 붙여서도 써요.
explain_en: The official name is '법학전문대학원', but in daily life people almost always say '로스쿨'. It is a graduate school for people who want to become legal professionals such as lawyers. You can also attach it to other words, as in '로스쿨생' or '로스쿨 입시'.

examples.ko: 같은 품목의 도매가와 소매가를 적어 두면 다음 소비가 쉬워진다.
examples.en: If you write down the wholesale and retail prices of the same item, next time's spending becomes easier.

examples.ko: 도매 시장에서는 소매점보다 훨씬 싼 값에 물건을 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: At a wholesale market you can buy things at a much lower price than at retail shops.

examples.ko: 동대문에는 옷을 도매로 파는 가게가 많아요.
examples.en: Dongdaemun has many shops that sell clothes wholesale.

examples.ko: 이 업체는 도매만 하고 개인에게는 팔지 않습니다.
examples.en: This company only does wholesale and doesn't sell to individuals.

examples.ko: 꽃 도매 시장은 새벽에 열려서 일찍 가야 좋은 꽃을 고를 수 있어요.
examples.en: The flower wholesale market opens at dawn, so you have to go early to pick good ones.

explain: 도매는 가게나 회사에 대량으로 파는 것이에요. 도매상, 도매가, 도매 시장처럼 붙여 써요.

phrases.example: 한두 명이 잘못했다고 전체를 도매금으로 비난하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: to lump everyone together and judge them all
phrases.en_equiv: to lump everyone together and judge them all

dict_examples.ko: 도매로 사면 한 개당 값은 싸지만 한꺼번에 많이 사야 해요.
dict_examples.en: Buying wholesale makes each item cheaper, but you must buy a lot at once.

explain_en: 도매 means selling in bulk to shops and companies. It's attached to other words: 도매상 (wholesaler), 도매가 (wholesale price), 도매 시장 (wholesale market).

examples.en: I left my umbrella in the classroom.
I left my phone at home.
I keep milk in the fridge.

examples.ko: 카페에 우산을 두고 와서 다시 갔어요.
examples.en: I left my umbrella at the café, so I went back.
Leave your bags here and look around.

explain: 놓다는 ‘내려놓는 동작’이고, 두다는 ‘그 자리에 계속 있게 하는 것’이에요. 그래서 물건을 잊고 왔을 때는 “두고 왔어요”라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: to take something to heart, to dwell on
phrases.nuance_en: used when you keep something in mind and cannot forget or let go of it
phrases.en_equiv: to take something to heart, to dwell on

explain_en: 놓다 is the act of putting something down; 두다 is about leaving it in place. That is why, when you forget something somewhere, you often say 두고 왔어요 (I left it there).

dis.h: leave or keep in a place

p.n: 놓다 stresses the act of setting it down.

examples.en: Outside the bus window, it was raining.
I looked out the window, and it was snowing.
I can hear children playing outside the window.
I was just looking out the window during class.
It's dangerous to stick your hand out of the window.

explain: 창밖은 한 단어라서 붙여 써요. ‘집 밖’은 띄어 쓰지만 ‘창밖’, ‘문밖’은 붙여 써요.

explain_en: 창밖 is one word, so no space. Compare 집 밖 (with a space) with 창밖 and 문밖 (written together).

examples.en: My friend is a lawyer.
I'm not a lawyer. I'm an office worker.
A lawyer knows the law well.
A lawyer reads documents in the office.
I'm going to meet a lawyer tomorrow.

explain: 변호사는 사람을 도와주는 법 전문가예요. 재판에서 판단하는 사람은 “판사”예요. 두 직업은 달라요.

explain_en: A 변호사 is a legal expert who helps a client. The person who decides a case in court is a 판사 (judge). They are different jobs.

examples.en: There was a small incident on the bus yesterday.
That incident was on the evening news.
The police are investigating that case.

examples.ko: 어제 우리 동네에서 큰 사건이 있었다고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard that a big incident happened in our neighborhood yesterday.

examples.ko: 그 사건 이후로 친구와 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: Since that incident, I haven't talked to my friend.

explain: ‘일’은 평범한 일에도 쓰지만 ‘사건’은 특별하거나 나쁜 일에 많이 써요. 뉴스에서는 ‘사건·사고’라고 함께 말해요.
explain_en: 일 can be anything, even ordinary things, but 사건 is mostly a special or bad event. In the news you hear them together as 사건·사고 (incidents and accidents).

examples.ko: 주간 날씨에서 주말 비 소식을 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked the weekly forecast and saw rain for the weekend.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 월요일마다 주간 회의를 해요.
examples.en: Our team has a weekly meeting every Monday.
I made the weekly plan together with the team.
I have to hand in the weekly report by Friday.
I checked the weekly bestsellers at the bookstore.

explain: '주간 보고'의 '주간'은 한 주예요. 근무에서 '주간·야간'이라고 하면 낮과 밤이라서 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: The 주간 in 주간 보고 means 'week'. In work shifts, 주간 and 야간 mean day and night, which is a different word with the same sound.

dis.h: weekly period; used in plans and reports

p.n: 주 cannot replace 주간 as a modifier here; 주간 means 'weekly'.

examples.en: I'm planning to move next month.
I moved over the weekend, so I'm exhausted.
My friend moved, so I'm going to buy a gift.
I'm going to move from Seoul to Busan.
When you move, you need new furniture.

explain: 떠나는 쪽에서는 “이사 가요”, 내가 있는 곳으로 올 때는 “이사 와요”라고 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 형님께서는 그 집을 팔고, 작은 집으로 이사하셨소.
dict_examples.en: Your elder brother sold that house and moved to a smaller one.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: From the side of the place you leave, say 이사 가요. When someone moves to where you are, say 이사 와요.

p.n: 이주하다 sounds like a bigger, more formal move to settle elsewhere.
